"Through an indirect source who is said to be reliable, we have acquired photocopies of the topographical maps which the KLA gave to American representatives in Macedonia on May 15th, 1999. "Drawn on the maps are the precise positions and coordinates of VJ and MUP units and also the areas which they are not allowed to target, areas where KLA units and Siptar refugees are situated. "Enclosed: Photocopies of topographical maps (5 pages)."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Were you familiar with this report received at the intelligence administration?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in general principle, yes. I did not -- I hadn't read the report, but I knew that such information was being forwarded.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, I would just like to ask you this: The verification mission and the locators, could you tell us what -- how efficient were the NATO air-strikes and how precise were they in targeting certain targets, and do you have any information as to how they were -- how the fire was directed and through what means this was done?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not have a lot of information for the period when the verification mission was there. I do have some information from the period at the beginning of the NATO air-strikes, but this was something that was really done by the intelligence organs so that I myself was not privy to the details. But I did learn at the command about some of these things. I learned, for instance, that the locators had been put in place and we could ascertain this for ourselves because the targeting was very, very precise. And we were, for instance, near a warehouse in Gracanica. We were some 150 metres away from the warehouse, and we never thought that they could miss the warehouse and hit us because they were so precise. And nearby was also a Serbian settlement, Gracanica, which numbered several thousand people. So there were no misses. They were very precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we admit this into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00349.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we have 65 ter list document 01614, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, sir, this is a document from the 3rd Army command, and I can see in the introductory paragraph that it was prepared pursuant to a warning sent from the staff of the Supreme Command. I suppose, because I see the initials here MC/MK, that you did not prepare this document?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not prepare this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But you were familiar with it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could we look at item 3, please.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 3 of this order says that because an aggression was impending, the fighting against Siptar terrorist forces should be conducted within the areas of responsibility; and if the terrorists are in that zone of responsibility, which means that if there should be artillery fire in the rear or from the flanks, in those cases unit commanders from the level of brigade and independent battalion should determine and allocate up to one-third of their forces for fighting these terrorist forces, whereas the brunt of their forces would conduct defensive operations. Because it was well-known that there would be a synchronised NATO and Siptar terrorist forces attack because they were in constant satellite contact. We know this for a fact. And their activities were synchronised and they would attack on the front line all elements of our combat disposition.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we admit this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00350.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, am I correct that as early as 15th of April there were incursions from Albania and attacks on our territory?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think those began already on the 9th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I think I actually prepared one of the reports for the General Staff, and I think this actually referred to two organised brigades of Siptar terrorist forces which made an excursion -- incursion from Albania in the mountainous area in the area of responsibility of the 53rd Border Guards Battalion, but these forces managed to actually close the gap after several kilometres of their advances. And then in systematic concentric fire they managed to push them back to the border with the Republic of Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us which mountain pass this is or which mountain border post? Was that Pastrik or --

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the area near the border post Morina, the mountainous area, the least passable area, and our forces were the thinnest there, which is actually why they actually chose to advance through that area because there was not much equipment there. Mostly these men were infantry fighters and they had some equipment with them, up to 72-millimetre mortars at most.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But later on was there another incursion in the area of Kosare from the Republic of Albania?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is the entire area that we're talking about towards the border with Montenegro, the area which is to the north-west of Djakovica, and I mean -- I'm referring to that mountain area, the Junik mountains actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, tell us, please, was this also an aware where weapons were smuggled and brought into the country in 1998?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was the main route for the supply of terrorist forces to Jablanica, where the main base is for these smuggled weapons was, and from there they were distributed to Srbica, Bajgora, towards the Milanovac -- Mount Milanovac, and Malisevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We did admit this into evidence, correct, this document 01614?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Not --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in that case, I tender it into evidence. I was just off with my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's the document that was assigned D00350.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that this is already an exhibit that it had number 350.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: One way or another it is D350.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see P44, please, Exhibit P44. The English version, page 3; in B/C/S I think it's page 2. Can we just have Article 17 in both versions, and can we just zoom in on them. Thank you. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, sir, this is Article 17 of the Law on Defence, and I'm sure that you're very familiar with it. But let us take a closer look at this article. Am I correct that in case of -- in a state of war, to be brief, units and organs of internal affairs can be used or may be used to carry out combat assignments?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In other words, if -- is this something that is conditional, it's not automatic, there is no automatic use of organs and units of the Ministry of the Internal Affairs?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they may be used to carry out combat assignments or rather to engage in combat or offer armed resistance, so these are two different things.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. Now -- next we see it says: "These units and organs carrying out their combat assignments shall be subordinate to the officer of the armed forces who is commanding combat operations;" correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So someone has to make a decision in order for this Article 17 to be applied; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, sir, are you aware that on the 18th of April, 1999, the supreme commander, the president of the FR, Slobodan Milosevic, issued an order on resubordination, not the use. Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but I seem to vaguely know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at Defence Exhibit D203.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Sir, the order in paragraph marked 1, does it state that units and organs of the Ministry of the Interior in the territory of the FR are to be resubordinated to the officers of the Yugoslav Army planning, organising, and commanding combat operations according to the tasks received in the assigned areas of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it states.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. And regardless of slight changes in the terminology more or less that would be that Article 17 according to the law, it would need to say the use of the forces, not resubordination of forces, the legal term is the use of forces?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the terminology is a little bit different.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But still that's what it is. So now we know. And in paragraph 2 we have: "The chief of the Supreme Command Staff will regulate by his order all other matters arising from item 1 of this order." And it is left up to General Ojdanic to regulate possible other matters; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now I'm going to ask you this: Where did you and when did you see for the first time the order of Mr. Ojdanic on the resubordination, or rather, the implementation of this order of the supreme commander, did you ever see this order before and when?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the morning -- in the afternoon of the 18th of April, I attended a meeting at which General Pavkovic had an order with him. But at that time I did not read it myself and I didn't know about it. Later, I found out the contents - this was after a certain period of time, let's say after a few days.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So on the 18th you knew that an order had been reached but you did not know exactly what the telegram said, you didn't read the telegram?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, I didn't read the telegram.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, it's not important whether on that day or the following day in April they came to Commander Pavkovic, where you were with a number of your colleagues, General Djordjevic, General Obradovic, and General Lukic from the MUP came to see him?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not Obradovic, but Obrad Stevanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Bravo, yes, thank you for the correction; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And that is when General Pavkovic issued -- gave General Djordjevic, who was sitting next to him, this telegram; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: At that time you didn't know the contents of the telegram?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And then you said that he read this telegram, General Djordjevic, for a minute or so and then he said what -- how come Ojdanic is resubordinating the MUP; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Djordjevic later, after he read it, said, What do you mean Ojdanic? Who is he supposed to be commanding? We didn't receive any order from the minister. And he returned the telegram to the general.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would I be correct if I said that judging by his reaction Djordjevic learned the contents of the telegram at that time, the telegram that was given to him by General Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is quite possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to look at exhibit on the 65 ter list 01460.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, for the record, the document is Exhibit P00887.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, sir, in paragraph marked with the number 1, what is General Ojdanic actually ordering?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In paragraph marked 1 General Ojdanic orders that internal affairs units and organs are to be subordinated to you in your areas of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And if -- can you please tell us whether it states that this applies to the time of combat, does it state that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you this, General: Does the Army of Yugoslavia -- or can the Army of Yugoslavia carry out assignments from the domain of the MUP that have nothing to do with armed battle which is, for example, apprehending those who committed crimes, matters that have to do with traffic, issuance of identity cards, passports, things that have nothing to do with the army?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the army cannot do that kind of job and is not authorised to do those kinds of jobs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: According to that Article 17 of the law and in the order of the supreme commander, it is specifically stated that units and the MUP organs be resubordinated in combat and not in other areas and competencies for which the MUP of the Republic of Serbia is authorised; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is possible only during combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But you cannot see that in this paragraph 1?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is not specified.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's not specified, as compared to the order of the president of the republic. And now, please, can you please look at the order -- the persons that the order is being dispatched to. Who is receiving this order?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is sent to the commander, then to the 3rd Army forward command post, to the Pristina Corps, to the commander of the Chief of Staff of the Pristina Corps, the Nis Corps, and to the commander also. I don't know to whom it refers, this note, "for information only."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. Is it stated anywhere that it's being sent to the minister of the interior or to any other organ of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there is nothing like that, but probably someone had to order the minister to draft the same kind of order or a similar order to pass it to the MUP staff and to other similar structures.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, this was supposed to be done, but we see in this order that this order was not provided to the MUP minister or anyone else?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but General Ojdanic is not authorised to order the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But he is authorised by the president of the republic in combat to resubordinate the units and the organs, and in order for them to know about this decision this decision had to be furnished to them. So Ojdanic's decision does not contain all that it's supposed to contain. How is the minister of internal affairs supposed to know who is the person in charge, and who's at the head of the ministry supposed to know that something like that has been adopted unless he is informed about it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, with this comment, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So we don't have it stated here that he has been informed, or we have the reaction of General Djordjevic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And now if you can please tell me, did you ever find out whether and when and if so who was informed of this decision by General Ojdanic at the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You don't know. All right. After receiving this - you said that you received this on the 18th -- well, let me just ask you this, please: Can you look at the stamp of the army command -- the incoming stamp of the army command, and then explain, if I'm seeing this properly, the strictly confidential number is 872 dated the 19th of September, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps we can look at the top of the page in the B/C/S. We only have one page. This page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it's dated the 18th of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, are you looking at the heading of the document?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the 19th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The 19th of April, yes. So was this received on the 19th of April technically and it has this number 94/2?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is logical. The telegram was delivered personally to General Pavkovic, the commander, who kept it with him and then when on the 18th he announced to the generals of the MUP that -- after they read it then he probably kept that with him for that evening still. And then the following day he sent it to be archived. And then the office stamped it because it received the document on the 19th. But at the bottom, in the receipt, the incoming stamp, you can see that the telegram arrived on the 18th of April, and I don't think there are any problems there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And just explain this to me, this 94/2, what does this slash 2 mean?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's probably indicating some sort of previous order that dealt with the same matter, the matter of resubordination or something like that, so that can be a document, document number 2, because the person who looks at number 872/94 probably will have something similar that has to do with resubordination and a document that was registered under number 94. But I don't know exactly what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, sir, after this, the commander of the 3rd Army also adopted an order or issued an order about resubordination, but the document refers to the execution of combat assignments.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at Exhibit D204.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this document? Did you work on this document?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: To whom was this document or this order sent?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was sent to the Pristina Corps and the commander of the PJP in Kosovo, General Lukic, and to the Nis Corps -- it was sent to them via communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to warn the Chamber, we're talking about Exhibit -- Defence Exhibit D205, and I think my learned friend Mr. Hannis used that yesterday. And it was marked P1238, but I think that this is the same document. This is General Lazarevic. It's also a decision on resubordination.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General Lazarevic implemented this order in detail. Would you agree with me, General, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he is being even more specific in defining the points.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And in paragraph 2 of item 4 he's saying: "At the time when there is no combat forces of the MUP are engaged to execute other specific tasks according to plans and orders of the MUP staff in Kosovo and Metohija." Am I correct that all of this is being conducted at the level of the brigades, the units that are carrying out combat activities, that the units and organs are to be resubordinated at that level? Can you please explain that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The corps commander cannot have so many units as the MUP had detachments, so in the -- in principle they are resubordinating those detachments to the brigades during the execution of combat actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So this is paragraph 5, resubordination of MUP forces to be carried out in combat operations in the areas of responsibility of the brigades by April 25, 1999?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat his question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you repeat your question, please, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So pursuant to paragraph marked 5, resubordination of MUP forces to carry out combat operations in the areas of responsibility of brigades would be carried out by the 25th of April, 1999, that is the level of resubordination?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you explain this now, please. Would this -- these orders, did the -- was the MUP staff resubordinated to anyone?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if the MUP staff was resubordinated because in principle an order did not define or specify the role of the MUP staff at the point in time when the units were being resubordinated to the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And now let me put it to you in a broader context. Is the MUP ministry in Belgrade resubordinated to anyone, because this order refers to the entire FRY not only to Serbia but also to the Montenegro MUP -- so the Montenegro MUP and the Serbian MUP. So I'm asking you: What is happening with the higher levels independent of Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about such an order, and we need not have necessarily received it there, because it relates to the role of the ministry and the MUP in Belgrade. All that was clear to us was that the combat sections of the MUP units during combat actions were being resubordinated to units of the Pristina Corps. And the decision on who was going where and who was being resubordinated to whom was exclusively in the domain of General Lazarevic in the area of responsibility of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell me the reports on the implementation of the assignments - we're talking about the 25th of April - that had to be -- that was the dead-line to be submitted to them, this referred to brigades?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So let me ask you this: If there are any problems in resubordination, up until the 25th of April the brigade commanders had to inform the Pristina Corps in their reports about it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In that case, would the Pristina Corps have to pass that up to the 3rd Army command, that there were problems in the resubordination?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: At the time, were you aware of any document regarding the problems in resubordination? We're talking about April. Did you receive such a document?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we knew that there were problems because units openly let know the commanders that they could not carry out the resubordination because they had not received any orders from the staff of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well -- but that's what I'm asking you. All of this what you're telling me about should be in the reports. Now, were these problems put in reports and was that sent to the corps and did the corps inform thereof the army command?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that General Pavkovic informed the General Staff and General Pavkovic personally that -- General Ojdanic personally that the units -- MUP units had not been resubordinated. And I also know that General Lazarevic was informed by his inferiors about this -- subordinates about this. But I'm not sure whether this was stated in each and every report.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But I'm asking you about any report. Now, was there any report that the army command received from the corps level that you know of?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I never really dealt with this problem, so I really wouldn't -- couldn't give you an answer. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you this: We said a few moments ago this had to be in the report from the Pristina Corps had it been written there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I know there were also reports sent via the communications system, the same type of information that was also put in written reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, let me now ask you: Do you know whether, in a report from the 3rd Army command which was sent to the Supreme Command Staff, whether there was a report sent to that effect in this period of time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, since I did not draft this combat report it would be difficult for me without a document to say anything off the top of my head. If I had a document, I could comment on it. Now, the -- I know that the report for the 3rd Army was drafted in Nis, not where I was. It was drafted by General Stojmirovic and the part of the unit that was in Nis, and they then forwarded reports to General Ojdanic about all these issues that were in the report, in the combat report.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I know that you did not do -- draft this because you were in Gracanica; however, in view of the position that you were on, had such a report come to Nis then it would have had to be further forwarded to the Supreme Command Staff; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you this, maybe you can clarify: Now if I were to look at all the reports from the Pristina Corps to the 3rd Army and then from the 3rd Army to the Supreme Command Staff, then I should be able to establish whether there were any such notes put in there; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see P1239. This is an exhibit that we saw yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That is a document that you drafted on the 8th of May, 1999, General. General, what was the purpose of drafting this document of the 8th of May, 1999?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order I drafted pursuant to General Pavkovic's order, and its purpose was to define more specifically the tasks assigned to MUP units and issues dealing with their resubordination, because the general on the 8th of May pursuant to a report from the commander of the Pristina Corps, he was aware that MUP had not been resubordinated up to that point to the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you just tell me, where can we find that in the introduction to this document?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this document did not state that, and that was not its purpose. This document had a wholly different purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, but if something is not in compliance, if an order is not complied with, and if we look at item 2, here it says: In order to completely destroy the remaining terrorist forces in your zones of responsibility and so on and then -- in order to prevent the further activities of STS and completely disarm terrorist groups and so on, and then it says "order." So what is the sense of this?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this -- the purpose of this was to tell General Lukic that he has to implement the order on resubordination and that it was not expected that no one could expect that this can be done in 24 hours, because the resubordination for combat activities also implied that there would be coordination, irrespective of the fact that they would be subordinated to the Pristina Corps anyway. So this is an exchange of communication between General Pavkovic and General Lukic whereby he was trying to tell General Lukic that he has to comply with this order because this order was received from the Chief of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you this: The activities that followed as of April 18th, 19th, and so on and so forth, were all these tasks actually carried out?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were carried out and there were never problems in carrying out tasks through coordination. So there was no issue there. We never received any sort of refusal from MUP. They never said that they would not take part in routing the Siptar terrorist forces. However, the problems arose because of the fact that the orders that were -- the order on resubordination was not completely clearly defined at the state level, not the way it should have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That's what I was aiming at. Now, looking at this document and all the other documents that we will still see, we've never seen any mention that there were any problems with resubordination during combat activities. Did you ever see any document of this type up until this date, the 24th of May, 1999?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now let's take a look at the next document, that's document P1214.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, this is a document issued by General Lazarevic on the 24th of May, 1999. Well, first let me ask you this: General Lazarevic is making a reference here to this order on resubordination, the order of the 18th and the order of the 3rd Army command of the 20th of April. There is no mention of any kind of the document that we've seen earlier, a little earlier, the one of the 18th of May, where you said that there were problems with resubordination.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they weren't sent to General Lukic as an order, but rather as a reminder that there was certain responsibilities and -- that were binding on him, but this was not a classic order on resubordination.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, if we look at paragraph 2 here it says that the commanders and commanders, komandir, of MUP are resisting and openly opposing of above mentioned obligations offering as a pretext the alleged lack of a corresponding order from their commander?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, but this is of the 24th of May. But we also saw the order of 20th of April and it was only, what, 34 days later that we see the first document where Lazarevic is actually informing Pavkovic of this?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is difficult for me to comment on this as to why there weren't any others, but I'm sure that General Lazarevic was aware as well as the government leadership, that they were aware that the resubordination had not been carried out. And General Lukic was -- had also been informed of this, but this would have had to be forwarded to the General Staff, just as General Lukic would have had to inform his minister of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, okay, let's not go into conjecture, but let's now take a look at a document P588 [sic]. General, this is a document from the 3rd Army. You did not draft this document. This is NV/NP, and as far as I could understand this this was done by General Pavkovic personally --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... P588 is a transcript. It can't be the right number.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I probably misspoke. It's 888, three 8s.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, can you see this document? Now we have it before us.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let's take a look at item 1 first. Here it is stated under A, where the reasons are given for something -- so there is a -- there is some kind of resubordination but not in keeping with the order. So what are the problems? A, the inherited peacetime autonomy of these units and the related conduct of their command personnel in practice, this is a reference to command of MUP units; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And under B it says: "The order of the NSVK, the Chief of Staff of the Supreme Command, was not accompanied by a corresponding order from the minister of the interior of the Republic of Serbia." So do you agree that this pin-points the problem that General Pavkovic exactly pin-pointed the problem and informed thereof the chief of the Supreme Command Staff?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but this is an order from the minister of the interior and not the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, exactly, you're correct. I made a mistake. So this is an order from the minister. So now let me ask you, the problem here is stated. Now, from this date up until the end of the war not much time passed. Now, do you know whether at any point anything was done in reference or with reference to this communication from General Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't know about this because I didn't receive any information from General Pavkovic and I didn't participate or prepare any -- or draft any document thereof.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And you didn't see any document relating to that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, as far as I can recall, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, the proposed measures here, let's zoom in on that, measures proposed, General Pavkovic is here proposing either that resubordination be carried out pursuant and in the spirit of that decision that was issued by the staff, that is one proposal; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And the alternative proposal is either to annul this order and to agree with the MUP staff via a Joint Command and work with them in this manner in the same way that it had been done earlier, that coordination was carried out earlier?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, tell me, please, from the time when this decision was adopted in April 1999, the decision by General Pavkovic, up until the end of the war or at least the 25th of May, 1999, there was no coordination between them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at this time I was at the forward command post in Gracanica, and during my testimony in the Milutinovic case I said that I wasn't able to actually follow the developments in this segment. I -- all I knew was that the resubordination had not been carried out and that after the 19th I was never issued any order or any tasks from General Pavkovic to take any measures in that sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I won't read now to you the documents that relate to this because you said you're not familiar with them, but let's move on. There is an interesting document I'd like to show you, that's Exhibit P961. P961. General, is this an order issued by the Pristina Corps commander of May 27th, 1999?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we look at the heading it would appear so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's take a look at number 2. We see the tasks of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we just scroll down the English version to see item 2 on the monitors so that the Trial Chamber and my learned colleague could see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So under 2 we see the Pristina Corps' task.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now please show us page -- page 4 of the English version and page 3 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Under 5, General, we see here 5.1 it says: "37th Motorised Brigade" and then "36th;" correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Then on the same page, on page 5 of the English version, we can see 5.3, paragraph 5.3, in addition to the 58th Light Infantry Brigade. We also see the 35th Detachment of the PJP; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to look at the last page, please, so that we can see that it's been signed by General Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: With this decision the -- General Lazarevic is using units of the Pristina Corps and the MUP in assignments pursuant to this order, am I -- pursuant to this command; am I correct, General?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, according to this you could say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please have P1234.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I have a very short question. You said that this was the format that you provided to the MUP staff in Pristina. Do you remember, did you give this form to -- as a template?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not get the name of the person the template was being given to. Could the counsel please repeat the name of the person in his question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: My question for the transcript, General -- I'm going to repeat the question again. Did you give this template of the 19th of February, 1999, to Dusan Adamovic who worked at the MUP staff in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, through the emergency -- or duty service, I did pass it on to Mr. Adamovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, we saw three documents yesterday of the federal defence ministry. I think these are documents that have to do with the chief of the administration, Mr. Ilic, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let us clarify one thing. Am I correct that the Army of Yugoslavia did not have any connections with the Federal Ministry of Defence and its staff units, the defence administration in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not have any jurisdiction in terms of issuing orders and could not have had such a jurisdiction.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So the -- they could not issue orders to one another; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Are you aware that or do you know if units of the police had tanks?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I correct that only combat groups that were in coordinated action with certain police units could have tanks?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tanks, yes, police units had armoured personnel carriers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I'm only asking you now about tanks.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not have tanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to -- I have another question. When carrying out combat actions - I'm just giving an example to make it easier - the commander of the 549th Brigade, Delic, and his units and the commander of the 37th Detachment let's say of the Nis PJP in practice, in order to coordinate at that level, was it usual for the deputy commander of the 37th Detachment would be with Mr. Delic and Mr. Delic's deputy would be with the commander of the 37th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are asking -- are you asking about conditions of resubordination or joint coordination?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No resubordination, just joint coordinated action. That's what I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This does not necessarily have to be done. It's not specified anywhere in the rules for the Chief of Staff of the brigade to go to the command post of the PJP units. This was not even a practical thing for the Chief of Staff who is the main organiser of the assignments in the command would be carrying out a kind of auxiliary duty to spend time at the command post of the police units. This would be a waste of forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't thinking of the Chief of Staff specifically in that role, but a person assigned to do that by the brigade commander. For example, Delic did go to -- into action, so perhaps he would allocate a person who would be together with the PJP commander at the position where he was and the deputy PJP commander would be with Delic. I'm not talking about rules, just in the execution of combat activities in order to achieve this coordinated action and the communication that you referred to.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot speak for Delic and how that was. If you ask me how I would have worked, I would establish communications with the PJP police commander, a certain -- specific communication, and together with him -- during combat, because he's not subordinated to me, we would keep informing each other back and forth about what was going on at the line of contact and what was going on along the depth. And in accordance with that we would be reaching decisions jointly. If he were subordinated, however, he would get a strict order, start moving in that direction, rout the forces, reach the line, and report back to me. That is the difference between the classical order and the coordinated action of units.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, thank you for answering to my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have completed my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If I may just have a moment to get organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, yesterday at page 7991, line 1, the Defence counsel asked you about the operation called Grom, Grom 98. And in your answer you said it was considered that this was directed by an inter-departmental staff. And after that we started with this Joint Command because this inter-departmental staff led by Mr. Stanisic somehow disbanded because they were not up to the task. My first question was: The Mr. Stanisic you're referring to there in connection with an inter-departmental staff was Jovica Stanisic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was Jovica Stanisic. I talked about the inter-departmental staff of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And inter-departmental staff within the MUP exclusively; is that what you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was the members of the state security, members of the police, and then later pursuant to the order of the commander of the army in these actions, Thunder, General Simic also was engaged who testified in the case against Mr. Milutinovic. I think it's him that we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. You were also asked about the plan to combat terrorism that was first approved by Mr. Milosevic, I think, on July 21st, 1998. And in asking you a question about it at page 7996, line 17, Mr. Djurdjic said: "I found out that this was called a global plan for the destruction of sabotage and terrorist forces." And I know that we've seen that term "global plan" in a -- in a MUP document, I think it's Exhibit P768 in evidence. Was that a term that you used in the VJ? Did you refer to it as a global plan?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The word "global" is not used in the army so much, but it's the same thing as a general plan. It's a plan that sets the -- establishes the basis on which other plans can be made, and on the basis of that orders can be issued. We did write "general" and "global." It's not a mistake, one or the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... line 9, Mr. Djurdjic asked if you ever saw any kind of decision on the establishment of a joint command and your answer was no. I'd like to show you an exhibit now. This is 65 ter number 01317. And I think this was shown to you during proofing. This is a document dated the 12th of July, 2002, it's from the Federal Ministry of Justice of the -- well, the document says the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia in response to a request for assistance from the Office of the Prosecutor, asking questions about the Joint Command. And you'll see the first bullet point. The information from the Serbian government is that: "The Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija was formed on the order by the FRY President in June 1998 without any specific document." You weren't present in June 1998 when Mr. Milosevic formed the Joint Command, were you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If this is correct, that would explain why --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, I see Mr. Djurdjic on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologised if I heard properly. This is a document from 2002 and the federal ministry is writing something in response to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's correct. Thank you. Carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If that information is correct, General, that would explain why you never saw a document creating the Joint Command; would you agree?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I didn't see it, definitely.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender 1317 at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01245.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: At page 8000, line 13, yesterday, Mr. Djurdjic asked you if the army ever carried out or implemented any decision by the Joint Command, and your answer was what you considered the Joint Command to be the decisions pertaining to those decisions issued by General Samardzic and you're absolutely certain that Pavkovic could not carry out any assignment or issue instructions without Samardzic being in on it. What about 1999? Did you ever attend any meetings of the Joint Command after October 1998? I'm sorry, did you answer? Did you attend any Joint Command meetings after October 1998?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. Only one meeting which I referred to on the 18th was when I was present, and it was also attended by members of the MUP and the army. I wasn't even engaged in the coordination because this was transferred to the jurisdiction of General Radojko Stefanovic, and I was not working on that. So I simply was not in a position to know, and I did not personally see any members that were registered on the 22nd of July, 2008, in the record other than Mr. Andjelkovic. I think I have said that already three or four times.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You said --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I see Mr. Djurdjic on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a brief objection for the purpose of the transcript. The -- Mr. Hannis made a conclusion and asked him whether he attended meetings of the Joint Command in 1999, but the witness did not even say if he knew that such a command existed in 1999. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think that evidence came from General Vasiljevic that there was a meeting of the Joint Command on the 1st of June, 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We have, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, in your answer you mention a meeting on the 18th of April. I think you're talking about the meeting where General Pavkovic gave General Ojdanic's order about subordination to General Djordjevic; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And that wasn't a meeting of the Joint Command like those 1998 meetings where the political persons like Mr. Minic and Mr. Sainovic and others were in attendance?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was just a meeting in order to provide information to the MUP members and to give them the order by General Ojdanic about resubordination. It wasn't a meeting that had particular format, didn't last more -- longer than 10 or 15 minutes all in all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the meetings in 1998 of the Joint Command that you attended and took notes, was there a person who seemed to be the chairperson in terms of running the meeting, you know, starting the meeting, discussing the agenda, ending the meeting, did anyone do that or did everyone just start talking at once? How did it work in real life?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was actually like this as it happened. As far as I know, it was not known when the next meeting would take place. There would be telephone contact between General Lukic and General Pavkovic, and then depending on the situation they would decide when the next meeting would be held. Upon arriving at the place where the meeting was being held, I noted down in the notebook that you saw that it was the first meeting of the Joint Command after going to the command and based on the explanation of General Pavkovic. All the other meetings I did also record - and you can see that from the notebook - as sessions because civilians called that "sednice," [phoen] a gathering, a session. It was never referred to as a meeting. In essence, there is no significant difference, but it's a term that is more suitable for the civilian structure than the military structure. And the agenda was written by me most often on the basis of the discussion, or it would happen sometimes that some of the civilians would say, I would like to discuss the protection of the cities a little bit today, the protection of the population, and other questions that General Pavkovic and General Lukic would also put forward for discussion, they would also be discussed. Most often the meeting would begin with the organs of the state security, would take quite a long time to present detailed information that they acquired through operations and technical -- by technical means about the activities of foreign intelligence services and the Siptar forces. So if you consider the time based on the analysis that I did, about 60 per cent of the time was spent on these intelligence reports. I wrote more detail about that, as much as I could manage, and I did my best to write that down because for objective reasons it was important to me at the command. And I also passed on some information to organs of the corps command depending on the nature of the intelligence, either I would pass it on to security organs, intelligence organs, or other organs. After Mr. Gajic and Mr. Radovic, most often then the floor would be given or he would begin to explain about what the police did over the past few days or what they planned to do in the future. That is the format of the meetings. After that it would be General Pavkovic. Depending on the matters that were being discussed, the others would then individually participate in the discussion and the debate. I often did not write down and it wasn't of much interest to me what Mr. Sainovic was saying about these international contacts because this was in the domain of politics, which to me as an officer didn't mean much in the resolution of the problems that I had and the corps command had. That is why I noted down the points of discussion, but he spoke much more, especially about the meetings with Mr. Hill, Miles, and the others, because he would also go to Macedonia for meetings, he would -- Mr. Hill would come to Kosovo, and they were practically resolving some political issues that I was aware of as problems but were not important to me as a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can I stop you there. I think we're close to our time for ending for the evening --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if I may I would like to continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, we have reached our time. We resume tomorrow morning at 9.00 so that the re-examination should continue then. We will adjourn now for the evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 20th day of August, 2009, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.00 p.m.,
